Its named, multi-slot +generalization is **template inheritance** (ADR-040): a base defines named +`{% block name %}…{% endblock %}` slots with default bodies, and a child +`{% extends "base" %}` overrides the ones it names — the rest keep their defaults. +`{% super %}` splices the parent block's body into an override. + +```maxbars +{% inline "base" %} +{% block title %}Site{% endblock %} +
{% block content %}{% endblock %}
+{% endinline %} +{% extends "base" %} +{% block title %}Welcome — {% super %}{% endblock %} {# → Welcome — Site #} +{% block content %}

Hi

{% endblock %} {# title's default is overridden, kept otherwise #} +``` + +Inheritance is **resolved statically at compile time** — a lower-phase flatten +(`Kernel.Inherit`, mirrored in Rust by `trussbars_template::inherit`) that walks the +`{% extends %}` chain leaf→root over the `{% inline %}` base registry, merges block +overrides (a leaf override wins over an ancestor's), and fills the root's slots into a +plain template. No inheritance node survives into the interpreter, the AOT-emitted Rust, +or the VM, so all three render byte-identically (conformance-gated).
